scope: Independent read-only code review of the four bounded provenance, insertion-camera, Carrier-flight and Musou-UI changes. Working-tree hashes below are the reviewed state, not a claim about a later clean release commit or browser run.

observations: 43 documentary identities are attached after the existing reference-card mapping, with non-enumerable, non-writable and non-configurable descriptors; local IDs, current kits and enumerable save data remain authoritative.
v1 entities/bindings and v2 nested reference arrays/records are frozen; own-key and string checks prevent inherited/prototype keys from resolving as identities.
character.yautja/item.yautja documentary IDs are separate from the773-row yhw: public registry namespace; no admission by name or runtime asset/faction mutation is introduced.
Integration documentation explicitly scopes the v2 unmerged status to its pinned historical snapshot rather than asserting a current remote PR state.
updateInsertionPresentation applies the existing physical camera solver after smoothing, independently for P1 and P2 with each actual near-plane radius, before lookAt.
The main update exits before this branch when paused, photo mode or weapon wheel is active; inactive insertion returns without writing ordinary or photo cameras.
The change writes camera positions only. It does not hide geometry, change player/nav contacts, capsule visibility phases, factions, resources or allocations.
The tests exercise the real GameApp methods, actual Val Verde geometry and capsule sequencing without the DOM/WebGL constructor, preserving both exit positions and geometry visibility.

The only production behavior change exempts an actor with an existing carrierFlight from Bridge walking-floor projection. Horde advances that authoritative finite arc; normal floor projection resumes when it clears at landing.
The final main update order is Horde.update→Bridge.sync→physical movement resolution. The new guard fixes the before-render snap at both the normal end-of-update sync and other sync calls.

No target selection or launch gate is widened: hostile faction, real owner entry, paused/result checks, defend radius 24, formation radius 28, launch radius 13, safe destination and line-of-sight remain in their owners.

Tests invoke the original borrowed Bridge callback through production Horde acquisition rather than an explicit launch request, and cover all six original cargo IDs plus absence of a seventh,952 IDs and cap 32.

Pause without Horde ticks keeps arc time/pose. The saved released UID and remaining cargo survive restoration as distant state; the rendered airborne interpolation itself is intentionally not claimed as persisted.
Compact map keys derive from stable configuration front order, which getHUDState preserves, rather than the changing danger-priority order. OperationPanel looks up keys by actual front ID.
Full source names remain in configuration, detailed report, briefing legend and accessible title/aria labels. Unknown control stays marked; no new enemy reserve/effectif disclosure is added.
Legend rendering uses DOM textContent and a signature to avoid rebuilding unchanged lists; text strokes are clamped to canvas bounds and responsive DOM containers hold the source paragraphs.

selectedLevel accessor updates selected and aria-pressed consistently. setOperationLevel disables only manual terrain-card selection while an authored operation owns its map, publishes an explanation and restores free card selection for free-terrain modes.

The actual setupOperationSelection now calls setOperationLevel(scene?level:null). Native disabled and the click-handler guard block contradictory clicks; direct checkpoint assignments and rebuilding card grids retain their path.
No signed scenario/front data, faction, allocations, HUD priority policy, combat damage or save schema is changed by the presentation helpers.

reviewFindings.finding: After selecting authored AFF-27, a subsequent manual terrain-card click could override the displayed selectedLevel while the operation/provenance still described its bound terrain, recreating the misleading selection.
reviewFindings.resolution: Owner introduced setOperationLevel, native button disabling plus handler guard, a user-facing bound-terrain notice and immediate re-enable on free-terrain mode; root wired the real operation-selection call.
reviewFindings.verificationScope: Read final runtime method/handler and the new actual-UI-method regression test. Owner 24-test log is recorded separately; independent reviewer did not execute it.

remainingValidationAndLimits: Root must bind the final clean runtime commit/source fingerprint to the final tests/build and actual browser evidence; this report cannot certify later source edits.

Final rendered QA remains separate: LV-742 menus/briefing/minimap in both desktop viewports, real autonomous Carrier flight in the authored operation, co-op insertion, and real checkpoint reload of the Ravager phase.
Physical camera boom clearance does not prove universal player/danger visibility; the P1 foreground-roof issue remains outside the four-line collision fix.
Carrier CPU tests use a flat physical test arena and existing LOS/landing gates; they do not certify every curved flight path against every dynamic or overhead obstacle on all maps.
Compact plan keys address long source labels in the scoped plans; no universal non-overlap, human readability or gamepad accessibility certification is inferred.
No claim that a separate user-mentioned Bible outside the available repository contract has been read.
No global AUD criterion is closed by this review; no human testers,1:1 fidelity or hardware performance certification.

guidesRead.application: Review principles only; project Musou contracts and Three r160 APIs remain authoritative.
